expectations.text: Contract comments at declarations in .h; .cc does not duplicate them
expectations.evidence: All contracts live in retry_queue.h; the .cc has exactly one comment, explaining the shift-based backoff computation.

expectations.text: Ownership of the raw payload pointer documented
expectations.evidence: Class comment: 'The queue never owns payload pointers; the caller must keep each payload alive...'; Schedule: 'Does not take ownership'; Entry.payload: '// Not owned.'

expectations.text: MarkFailed's nullopt ambiguity documented (unknown OR dropped)
expectations.evidence: 'or std::nullopt if the task is unknown or has now reached max_attempts and been dropped', plus payload-cleanup responsibility.

expectations.text: DrainReady documents removal of drained tasks
expectations.evidence: 'Returned tasks are forgotten unless the caller re-Schedules them.'

expectations.text: Class comment explains purpose (usage/thread-safety a plus)
expectations.evidence: Class comment covers purpose, backoff semantics, caller-supplied clock design, a usage example, and an explicit 'Not thread-safe' statement.

expectations.text: Member variables with non-obvious semantics commented (units, meanings)
expectations.evidence: base_delay_s_ '(in seconds)', Entry fields including ready_at_s meaning and payload ownership.

expectations.text: // style, no Author: lines, no code-restating comments
expectations.evidence: Consistent //; no Author line; the single .cc comment explains the shift trick rather than restating it. The usage example even uses /*param=*/ argument comments.
